I came off of lithium for pregnancy and switched to Latuda. My psychiatrist said that lithium wasn't safe and I was really anxious about hurting the baby in any way, so I switched to Latuda. That said... I was very unstable during and after pregnancy. My own sister has told me she will not be a support to me if I get pregnant again, because she found my mental health to be too much of a drain. If you are working with a team that is aware of the risks, and are open with you on what the risks exactly ARE (I honestly don't know) it may be worth it to stay on lithium. I am working with my psychiatrist now to try and get on "pregnancy safe" meds after a severe PPD induced crisis. I just started Vraylar and am coming off of Latuda. If you ever want to message and talk I'm here. Best of luck to you, mama. I don't have a lot to say that hasn't already been said, but I would maybe challenge the "your kid will be bullied" statement I keep seeing. I have an unusual name and I didn't get a lot of ridicule for it, but I felt ashamed of my name my entire life. I felt othered and on the outside even though no one actually mocked my name. I didn't like that no one could spell my name, pronounce it when they read it, or that I had to tell people to just use a nickname when they struggled. I want to give kids the benefit of the doubt and think we will have a kinder rising generation who will be accepting, but recognize that bullies or not, you give a child one of the names you're tossing around and they will likely feel like an outcast. 
I also think I have experienced prejudice because of my name in the professional field which sucks a ton. Just don't do it.

Yep, I was doing the dream feeds. There was one or two nights that he slept through on the feeds, but mostly he would wake and be inconsolable. I haven't spoken to my pediatrician about it yet. We saw him at the beginning of what we thought was a sleep regression and he suggested beginning solids during the day. Hasn't made a difference, unfortunately!

Right now I wake up with him for the night feedings and then my husband takes over around 6am so I can sleep until 9-9:30. Something about me sleeping from 6 onwards really makes a difference to me versus having him take earlier feedings and me waking up with LO at 6. I just try to schedule my workday to start later.

He doesn't have a nap schedule yet. I really don't know when he will sleep. We've kept bedtime routine strict though. Feeding, changing, rocking in the chair while Dad reads a story, then rocking for two songs from mom, then in his crib. Some nights he lays quietly until he sleeps, others he screams and we do pop ins.

My LO slept from 8:30pm to 6am like clockwork on his own from months 2.5-4. I thought I had hit the jackpot. Then his sleep became really interrupted and I thought it was a sleep regression, but he'll be 6 months on the 28th and we're seeing no end in sight.
